q: 1. The ratio of specific weight of a liquid to the specific weight of pure water at a standard temperature is called
explain: Specific gravity (S) is a dimensionless ratio comparing a liquid's density or specific weight to that of a standard fluid (water at 4°C).

q: 2. A glass tube of smaller diameter is used while performing an experiment for the capillary rise of water because
options: it is easier to see through the glass tube
glass tube is cheaper than a metallic tube
it is not possible to conduct this experiment with any other tube
explain: While small diameters increase the height of capillary rise (making it measurable), glass is used specifically for its transparency to allow for clear observation of the meniscus.

q: 3. The height of a water column equivalent to a pressure of 0.15 MPa is
explain: h = P / w. Converting 0.15 MPa to 150 kPa: 150 / 9.81 ≈ 15.3 m.

q: 4. A piezometer tube is used only for measuring
explain: Piezometers are unsuitable for very high pressures (tube would be too long) or vacuum pressures (air would enter the tube).

q: 5. The liquid used in manometers should have
explain: High-density liquids (like mercury) allow for shorter manometer tubes when measuring high pressures.

q: 6. The centre of pressure for a vertically immersed surface lies at a distance equal to _________ the centre of gravity.
explain: The centre of pressure always lies below the centre of gravity because pressure increases with depth.

q: 7. In a lockgate, the reaction between two gates is
explain: The reaction R at the hinge/meeting point is calculated as P / (2 sin α) based on force equilibrium.

q: 8. The water pressure per metre length on a vertical masonary wall of dam is
explain: This follows the same logic as Q.38 for the total hydrostatic force on a vertical surface.

q: 9. When a body is placed over a liquid, it will sink down if
options: gravitational force is equal to the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is less than the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is more than the upthrust of the liquid
explain: If the downward weight exceeds the upward buoyant force, the body will have a net downward acceleration.

q: 10. When a body is immersed wholly or partially in a liquid, it is lifted up by a force equal to weight of liquid displaced by the body. This statement is called
explain: This is the fundamental definition of Archimedes' Principle regarding buoyancy.

q: 11. When a body, floating in a liquid, is given a small angular displacement, it starts oscillating about a point known as
explain: The Metacentre is the point of intersection of the vertical through the new centre of buoyancy and the original axis of the body.

q: 12. A flow in which the quantity of liquid flowing per second is constant, is called _________ flow.
explain: Steady flow is defined as flow where properties (like discharge/velocity) do not change with respect to time.

q: 13. The increase in pressure at the outer edge of a drum of radius (r) completely filled up with liquid of density (ρ) and rotating at (ω) rad/s is ............
explain: The pressure difference between the center and a point at radius $r$ in a forced vortex is $\Delta P = \frac{\rho \omega^2 r^2}{2}$.

q: 14. One stoke is equal to ............
15. The unit of kinematic viscosity in S.I. units is ............
explain: The SI unit for kinematic viscosity is square meters per second ($m^2/s$).

q: 16. Water is a ............ fluid.
explain: Water, air, and thin oils are common examples of Newtonian fluids.

q: 17. The shear stress-strain graph for a Newtonian fluid is a ............
explain: Since $	au \propto du/dy$, the relationship is linear and passes through the origin.

q: 18. Hydrostatic pressure on a dam depends upon its ...............
explain: According to the hydrostatic law (P = ρgh), the pressure depends solely on the vertical depth below the free surface and the density of the liquid.

q: 19. Gauge pressure is ...............
explain: Gauge pressure is measured relative to atmospheric pressure. Therefore, Absolute Pressure = Gauge Pressure + Atmospheric Pressure.

q: 20. The total pressure force on a plane area is equal to the area multiplied by the intensity of pressure at its centroid if ...............
explain: The total force F = P_avg × A. For any submerged plane, the average pressure occurs at the depth of the centroid (h_bar), regardless of orientation.

q: 21. The centre of pressure of a vertical plane immersed in a liquid is at ...............
explain: The center of pressure (h_p) is always located below the centroid of the area because pressure increases with depth.

q: 22. On an inclined plane, centre of pressure is located ...............
explain: Similar to a vertical plane, the pressure distribution is deeper at the bottom, shifting the resultant force (center of pressure) below the centroid.

q: 23. The rise of the liquid along the walls of a revolving cylinder above the initial level, is ...............
options: greater than the depression of the liquid at the axis of rotation
lesser than the depression of the liquid at the axis of rotation
the same as the depression of the liquid at the axis of rotation
explain: In a forced vortex (solid body rotation), the volume of the paraboloid of revolution is half the volume of the circumscribing cylinder, meaning rise = fall.

q: 24. If velocities of fluid particles vary from point to point in magnitude and direction, as well as form instant to instant, the flow is said to be ...............
explain: Turbulent flow is characterized by chaotic changes in pressure and flow velocity, varying both in space and time.

q: 25. The flow in which each liquid particle has a definite path and the paths of adjacent particles do not cross each other, is called ...............
explain: In streamline (or laminar) flow, fluid particles move in smooth layers or paths without macroscopic mixing.

q: 26. The differential equation dp/ρ + gdz + vdv = 0 for a fluid motion is suggested by ...............
explain: This is Euler's equation of motion. When integrated along a streamline, it yields the Bernoulli equation.

q: 27. The line joining the points to which the liquid rises in vertical piezometer tubes fitted at different cross-section of a conduit, is known as ...............
options: pressure grade line or hydraulic grade line
explain: The Hydraulic Grade Line (HGL) represents the sum of the pressure head and datum head (P/w + z) along the pipeline.

q: 28. From a nozzle exposed to atmosphere, the liquid jet traverses ...............
explain: A free jet acts as a projectile; under the influence of gravity, its trajectory follows a parabolic path.

q: 29. An ideal fluid ...............
explain: An ideal fluid is a theoretical concept where the fluid has no viscosity (frictionless) and is perfectly incompressible.

q: 30. If H is the depth of water retained by a vertical wall, the height of centre of pressure above the bottom is ...............
explain: The centre of pressure for a rectangular surface (vertical wall) is at $2/3 H$ from the top, which is $1/3 H$ (H/3) from the bottom.

q: 31. The hydrostatic law states that rate of increase of pressure in a vertical direction ...............
options: is equal to density of the fluid
is equal to specific weight of the fluid
is equal to weight of the fluid
explain: The hydrostatic law ($dp/dz = w$) states that the rate of pressure increase in the downward vertical direction is equal to the specific weight ($w$ or $\gamma$) of the fluid.

q: 32. Gauge pressure at a point is equal to ...............
explain: Gauge pressure is measured relative to local atmospheric pressure. Thus, Absolute Pressure = Gauge Pressure + Atmospheric Pressure.

q: 33. Atmospheric pressure head in terms of water column is ...............
explain: Standard atmospheric pressure ($101.325 kPa$) corresponds to a column of water approximately 10.3 meters high.

q: 34. For a submerged body, if the centre of buoyancy is above the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is...
explain: A submerged body is stable only when its centre of gravity ($G$) is below its centre of buoyancy ($B$).

q: 35. For a submerged body, if the meta-centre is below the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is called
explain: The concept of 'metacentre' is primarily used for floating bodies. For a fully submerged body, stability depends on the B and G relationship. Since the answer key specifies 'none of the above', it indicates that metacentric height rules for floating bodies don't apply here in the same way.

q: 36. If the velocity in a fluid flow changes with respect to length of direction of flow, it is called
explain: When velocity changes with respect to distance along the flow path, it is called non-uniform flow. Since non-uniform is not in the options, 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 37. Study of fluid motion without considering the forces causing the flow is known as
explain: Fluid Kinematics focuses on describing the motion of fluids (velocity, acceleration) without reference to the forces involved.

q: 38. The difference of pressure head (h) measured by a mercury-oil differential manometer is given as
explain: When the manometric liquid (Sg) is heavier than the flowing liquid (So), the pressure head difference is h = x[(Sg/So) - 1], where x is the difference in mercury levels.

q: 39. An oil of specific gravity 0.7 and pressure 0.14 kgf/cm² will have the height of oil as
explain: Pressure P = ρgh. Converting 0.14 kgf/cm² to kgf/m² gives 1400. Density of oil = 0.7 × 1000 = 700 kg/m³. Height h = 1400 / 700 = 2 meters.

q: 40. Froude's number (Fe) is given by
explain: Froude's number is defined as the ratio of inertia force to gravity force, mathematically expressed as Fr = V / √(gL).

q: 41. Terminal velocity of a falling body is equal to
options: the maximum velocity with which body will fall
the maximum constant velocity with which body will fall
explain: Terminal velocity is reached when the sum of the drag force and buoyancy equals the downward force of gravity, resulting in zero acceleration and constant velocity.

q: 42. Laminar sub-layer exists in
explain: Even in a turbulent boundary layer, there is a very thin region extremely close to the wall where viscous forces dominate and the flow remains laminar; this is the laminar sub-layer.

q: 43. The separation of boundary layer takes place in case of
explain: Boundary layer separation occurs in the presence of an adverse (positive) pressure gradient (dp/dx > 0), where the fluid is moving against increasing pressure.

q: 44. In sonic-flow, the disturbances, created by a projectile, moves
explain: In sonic flow, the projectile and the pressure disturbances it creates travel at the same speed, so they move together.

q: 45. For sub-sonic flow, if the area of flow increases
explain: In subsonic flow (Mach < 1), a diffuser (increasing area) causes the velocity to decrease and the pressure to increase, as per the continuity and Bernoulli principles.

q: 46. For super-sonic flow, if the area of flow increases, then
explain: In supersonic flow (Mach > 1), the relationship between area and velocity is inverted: an increase in area actually causes an increase in velocity.
